parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Lithium nitrate, $\text{LiNO}_3$, decomposes on heating in a similar way to Group 2 nitrates to give the metal oxide, a brown gas and oxygen.

Write an equation for the decomposition of $\text{LiNO}_3$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The other Group 1 nitrates, $\text{MNO}_3$, decompose on heating to form the metal nitrite, $\text{MNO}_2$, and oxygen.

The thermal stability of these nitrates increases down the group.

Suggest why the thermal stability of $\text{MNO}_3$ increases down the group.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Acidified manganate(VII) ions, $\text{MnO}_4^-$, can be used to analyse solutions containing nitrite ions, $\text{NO}_2^-$, by titration.

**X** is a solution of $\text{NaNO}_2$.

$250.0\text{ cm}^3$ of **X** is added to $50.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.125\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-(\text{aq})$. The $\text{MnO}_4^-(\text{aq})$ ions are in excess; all the $\text{NO}_2^-$ ions are oxidised in the reaction.

The unreacted $\text{MnO}_4^-(\text{aq})$ required $22.50\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0400\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq})$ to reach the end-point.

The relevant half-equations are shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Calculate the concentration, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{NaNO}_2$ in **X**.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Table 2.1 shows electrode potentials for some electrode reactions involving manganese compounds.

Table 2.1

| electrode reaction | $E^\ominus / \text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Mn}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Mn}$ | -1.18 |
| $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Mn}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.23 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ | +0.56 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^- + 4\text{H}^+ + 3\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.67 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.52 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^- + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{OH}^-$ | +0.59 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{OH}^-$ | +0.60 |
| $\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.70 |
parts.text:
Aqueous manganate(VI) ions, $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$, are unstable in acidic conditions and undergo a disproportionation reaction.

The $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$ for this reaction is $+1.14\text{ V}$.

Construct an overall ionic equation for this disproportionation reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain how the $E_{\text{cell}}$ value of the disproportionation reaction changes with an increase in pH.
